clue.text: Superior stock fear her presence when aroused

indicators.note: being aroused stirs things up, so these three words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is warned that a lover's presence will provoke fear once they are roused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when aroused' shuffles the fifteen letters of FEAR HER PRESENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A preference share is a class of company stock whose holders are paid dividends before ordinary shareholders, so it ranks higher.

clue.text: Calm account provided in movie

indicators.note: in puts the account and the condition inside the film

parts.note: pic is informal for a movie, a picture
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A tranquil story is included in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacific means peaceful or tranquil, from the Latin for peacemaking.

clue.text: Dress in ermine, standing up in novel bonnet

indicators.note: standing up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman wears ermine and stands, crowned by a new bonnet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'standing up' reverses the letters, which are found inside 'novel bonnet' read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers wear ermine-trimmed robes, so dressing someone in ermine figuratively makes them a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Rue inept learner clumsily advancing business

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, describing someone pushing business forward

indicators.note: clumsily suggests something done awkwardly, so these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A trainee regrets their awkward, incompetent start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsily' rearranges the fifteen letters of RUE INEPT LEARNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enterprising in commerce means taking risks to start and grow companies, i.e. promoting trade.

clue.text: Captain in Eastern sea showing relief

indicators.note: in places the chief inside the direction and the sea

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
a boss is a captain or leader, as in captain of industry

explanation.surface: A ship's captain in eastern waters looks relieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' looks like an emotion but is a raised design, as in relief carving.
explanation.definitionFit: Embossed work has a design raised from the surface, which is what relief means in art.

clue.text: Greek island retaining leftist systems of belief

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the island keeps the leftist inside it

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
a red is a communist or leftist

explanation.surface: A Greek island keeps hold of left-wing ideologies.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed sets out the tenets someone holds, such as a statement of faith.

clue.text: Senate attempt to revolt including leaders of Democrats and Republicans in branch of US government

indicators.note: to revolt is to rise up and overturn, so the letters are turned into a new order
leaders are the first letters of the following two words

explanation.surface: The US Senate tries a rebellion with help from both parties' leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to revolt' shuffles SENATE ATTEMPT with D and R, the first letters taken by 'leaders of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The State Department is the US federal department handling foreign affairs, a branch of the executive.

clue.text: Excite special quality in semiprecious stone

indicators.note: in places the pronoun for special quality inside the gemstone

parts.note: agate is a banded semiprecious stone
it means sex appeal or a special quality, as in 'she has it'

explanation.surface: A gemstone with a certain something thrills the buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate someone is to stir them up or disturb them.

clue.text: Beg companion to be excused from ballet manoeuvre

indicators.note: being excused from something means leaving it, so the companion's letters leave the leap

parts.note: an entrechat is a ballet leap with the feet crossed several times
CH stands for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A dancer pleads to be let off performing a difficult ballet move.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, for Companion of Honour, a British award, is the convention for companion.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead with or implore someone earnestly.

clue.text: Policeman on street intercepting urgent message

indicators.note: intercepting means one thing gets in the way of another, here the message is cut into by the other pieces

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, the old way of sending an urgent message

explanation.surface: An officer on the beat catches a pressing telegram as it is being delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is the lowest rank of police officer in Britain, an ordinary policeman.

clue.text: Boxer's time in top tier of celebrities

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the boxer, so the boxer's is Ali's

explanation.surface: A champion boxer's moment has come and he is now among the most famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the informal ranking of the most sought-after stars, the first rank of fame.

clue.text: False tale about strength of character

parts.note: a fib is a small lie, a false tale
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Someone tells a lie concerning a person's moral strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral fibre is resilience and toughness of personality, so fibre alone can mean strength of character.

clue.text: Novel article in shop, kind of ceramic

indicators.note: in places the new item and the article inside the word for a shop

parts.note: a store is a shop
novel as an adjective means new
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A shop displays a new item made of a type of pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but works as the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware is a dense, hard type of pottery fired at high temperature.

clue.text: Calls to package the woman's fruit

indicators.note: to package something is to wrap it up, so the calls enclose the pronoun

parts.note: cries are calls or shouts
her is the possessive for the woman

explanation.surface: Market traders shout as they bag up a woman's fruit purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherries are small stone fruits, so the plural noun fits fruit used as a collective.

clue.text: Religious education needed by man who has big shoes to fill?

definitions.text: who has big shoes to fill?
definitions.note: read as 'one who has big shoes to fill', a noun

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
a gent is a man, short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A man stepping into a demanding role needs some religious instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: a stand-in ruler has a monarch's footsteps to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules in place of an absent or underage monarch, so must live up to a royal predecessor's standard.

clue.text: Old King's rule for salad item

parts.note: Old King Cole is the nursery rhyme monarch, so his is Cole's
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A decree by a merry old monarch about what goes into a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the 'merry old soul' of an English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is shredded raw cabbage in dressing, a side salad dish.

clue.text: Back round university, indolent

indicators.note: round means the backbone wraps around the abbreviation for university

parts.note: the spine is the back, or backbone

explanation.surface: A lazy student lounges around the campus with an aching back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' suggests lying on one's back, which supine also means, but here it is the spine.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine literally means lying face up, and figuratively passive or lazy, failing to act.

clue.text: Whole lot chanted about Hebrews

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the past of sing goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: sang means chanted
Heb is the abbreviation for the Epistle to the Hebrews

explanation.surface: A choir intones songs about the Hebrew people.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole shebang is an informal idiom for everything, the entire affair.

clue.text: Country-lover's colourful display topped by Irishman

indicators.note: in a down answer, being topped by puts the Irishman above the display

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is the stock Irishman of crosswords
a riot of colour is a vivid display

explanation.surface: A nationalist's bright show is headed by a man from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country-lover' looks like a fan of rural life, but means someone who loves their nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is a person devoted to their nation, someone who loves their homeland.

clue.text: Sentimental upright type given endless credit

parts.note: roman is the upright typeface, as opposed to slanting italic

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for credit is dropped

parts.note: on tick means on credit, so tick is credit

explanation.surface: A soppy, honest character is offered credit that never runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright type' looks like a moral person but is printing type; 'endless' cuts TICK to TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic describes someone given to idealised feelings of love, i.e. soppy and emotional.

clue.text: Agree to restrict nasty smell made by piece of furniture

indicators.note: to restrict is to confine, so the agreeing word confines the smell

parts.note: to tally is to agree or correspond
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: People agree to curb an unpleasant odour coming from a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tallboy is a tall chest of drawers, a type of furniture.

clue.text: Two refreshing cups taken by high-class country house

parts.note: cha and tea are two words for a cup of tea
U means upper-class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

explanation.surface: A posh person drinks two cups of tea at a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is slang for tea, so the cups give CHA and TEA together.
explanation.definitionFit: A château is a French castle or large country house.

clue.text: Swimmer married in elegant room

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for married within the room

parts.note: a salon is an elegant reception room

explanation.surface: A wedding takes place in a stylish reception room.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmon is a fish, and crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

clue.text: Supporters get mad gathering in honour of United

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so the word for get mad collects the other pieces

parts.note: enrage, read loosely, is to make or get mad
to, as in a toast 'to the bride', means in honour of
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: Football fans grow angry at a celebration held for Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: TO means in honour of as in raising a glass to someone; 'gathering' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants or followers around a famous person, a band of supporters.

clue.text: Rectified insult after scrapping in a US city

indicators.note: rectified means put right, so the remaining letters are set in a new order
scrapping means discarding, so the two letters of in are thrown out of insult

explanation.surface: An insult has been corrected after something was scrapped in an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after scrapping' leaves SULT, which 'Rectified' reorders; the city's A is then added from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a large city in Oklahoma in the United States.

clue.text: In trial I bid case for acquittal

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A defendant in court makes a bid for an argument that will get them acquitted.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence that one was elsewhere at the time, a case for being found not guilty.

clue.text: Easily persuaded man to take up jangling a bell

indicators.note: to take up is to absorb or accommodate, so the word for man holds the jumbled letters

parts.note: a male is a man

indicators.note: jangling suggests a noisy jumbled sound, so the letters of a bell are shaken up

explanation.surface: A man is told to start ringing a bell, discordantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jangling' scrambles the letters of the bell phrase, which 'to take up' then holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Malleable literally describes metal that can be hammered into shape, and figuratively a pliable, easily influenced person.

clue.text: Enjoy your company, but clear off

definitions.meaning: to be on friendly terms with you
an old-fashioned dismissal meaning go away or don't talk nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can mean being on good terms with you, or be a brisk, dismissive exclamation telling someone to go.
